page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing 1 physical core and 2 threads. The processor cache hierarchy consists of 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core CPU execution alongside constrained multi-core and memory subsystem capabilities. The stress-ng single-core test yields a score of 1827.69, which sits in the average tier. Conversely, the stress-ng multi-core score of 1875.88 and the Geekbench multi-core score of 1321.0 are positioned in the lower performance brackets. Memory bandwidth is limited, with uncached large-block read speeds of 13.86 GB/sec and write speeds of 11.77 GB/sec. Single-threaded operations, such as gzip compression at 23.53 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 7.99 GB/sec, also reflect moderate to weak throughput.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the n2-highmem-2 is its high memory allocation relative to its limited compute capacity. While it provides a cost-effective entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing, it performs poorly in compute-bound tasks. Passmark database operations scored 716.3, and static web serving throughput reached 1.61 GB/sec. This instance is best suited for small-scale databases, memory-cached applications, lightweight enterprise applications, and basic utility workloads requiring more memory than compute.
